levelIdentity.cefrMappingCaveat: Per curriculum-master-a1-c2.md section 3, these are a working correspondence used to keep A1's design honest about what 'A1' means, not a certified CEFR alignment. LinguaChat's A1 is textual/interactive only; no listening, speaking or pronunciation descriptor is claimed as covered until those systems are implemented and tested (master contract section 13; CLAUDE.md voice/media boundary).

canDo: talk about their own everyday life in the present: what they do, where they live, how their day goes and roughly when
say who the people around them are and what those people are, simply
find their way in a place: ask where something is and understand a short answer
handle a small purchase end to end: choose, ask the price, understand the number, pay
say what they can and cannot do, and ask the same of someone else
arrange to meet somebody at a day, a time and a place
keep a conversation alive when they meet unknown language, by asking what a word means or how to say something
cannotYet: talk about the past in any form
talk about the future beyond a present-tense arrangement with a time word
give or follow directions of more than one step
explain a reason with a subordinate clause
describe people or places in more than one attribute
spell aloud, handle dates or months, or give personal contact details
sustain a conversation that changes topic more than once

cefrCaveats.arrangeToMeet: Fixing a day/time/place with no unexpected complication is a reasonable A1-band task, but 'arranging to meet' in CEFR terms typically sits closer to the A2 'goal-oriented co-operation' family once negotiation or an unexpected problem is involved. This capability is deliberately kept inside A1's tight ceiling — no negotiation, a scripted counter-proposal at most, all language already taught elsewhere in the level (a1-blueprint.json: 'Nothing new is needed to say it — which is the point') — but LC-BP-A2 and LC-AUD-001 must confirm A2's own 'making arrangements' capability (if any) is a genuine complexity increase (handling an unexpected change, negotiating between two options) and not a restatement of this one.

intentStrategy.rule: One intent per communicative function. Variants travel as a subtype on the step payload, the way Pre-A1 already carries repairKind, quantityForm and thingId — not as a new intent.

newSubtypesOnExistingIntents.change: level-aware taught range so 11-100 counts as target evidence in A1 while Pre-A1 keeps 1-10

intentStrategy.explosionGuard: If an arc's design needs more than three new intents, the arc is teaching phrases rather than a capability.

evaluationStrategy.rule: The canonical frame is always judged locally. Escalation is for a reply that is inconclusive, exactly as Pre-A1 routes it. No capability is designed to depend on the provider being reachable.
evaluationStrategy.evidenceEnforcement: check:hybrid-evaluation and check:repair-evaluation are the runtime gates that prove the evaluator rejects nonsense per intent (level QA acceptance item 4); this reconciliation does not re-derive per-intent nonsense/near-miss/wrong-meaning example sets, since inventing them without reading the runtime evaluator would risk contradicting what actually ships.

reuseMatrix.legendSource: docs/curriculum/a1-blueprint.json (I introduced, R reused-and-evaluated, C consolidated in an integrated conversation)
reuseMatrix.legendMappingToTemplate: check:a1-arc2 through check:a1-arc5 require every R/C mark to be EXERCISED BY A STEP, not merely recognised — stricter than the template's minimum. An R or C mark in an arc later than the introducing arc satisfies the template's T (transfer: new situation, same capability, per master contract section 6 'topics are contexts, not curriculum') by construction, because every A1 arc is a distinct communicative situation. A C mark additionally satisfies F (fluency: no new language, held together) and, on the closing arc, D (delayed retrieval across a real arc gap). A separate G (guided-only reuse) row does not exist in A1's matrix because guided-only mentions are not counted as reuse evidence at all.
reuseMatrix.mitigation: The three thin rows are all in the transactions branch. ask_the_price and buy_something return in the closing arc only as receptive input, so the review scheduler carries them; ask_about_getting_somewhere is a should-have and is the first candidate to drop if the level needs trimming.

early.modelAnswer: available while a frame is new, withheld on the arc's last recall

mid.modelAnswer: withheld on the integrated episode of each arc
mid.repair: required by design in at least one episode per arc

late.modelAnswer: withheld by default; support returns after a wrong answer

autonomy.principle: Phase is a design expectation, not a rule the engine applies. The support engine keeps deciding from this learner's evidence, exactly as it does in Pre-A1 — per master contract section 10, no level-specific implementation may bypass the central scaffolding logic.

mapping.recognition: comprehension steps (scene, model, comprehension, choice) — the learner understands/chooses
mapping.guidedProduction: word_order, fill_blank, guided_reply steps — substantial supplied structure
mapping.openAssistedProduction: free_reply/recall attempts where the shared scaffolding engine recorded a hint, model or suggestion used — see docs/curriculum/adaptive-support.md
mapping.openIndependentProduction: free_reply/recall/story-reply attempts with no support used; this is the canDos[].evidence.independent count in the live blueprint, a LEVEL target, not an arc-exit requirement (see docs/curriculum/a1-authoring-contract.md 'independent: 2 is a level target, not an arc exit')
mapping.transfer: an R or C mark in the reuseMatrix in an arc later than the capability's introducing arc — a genuinely new situation exercising the same capability
mapping.delayedRetrieval: the shared spaced-review scheduler across sessions, extended from Pre-A1's overdue-review rule to the A1+Pre-A1 union (see exitCriteria.readinessDimensionsForA2)

evidenceModel.graduationRule: A1 cannot graduate a learner using only recognition or guided production (master contract section 9). Required capabilities need independent (openIndependentProduction) evidence AND transfer evidence; exact numeric thresholds are deliberately not fixed yet — a1-blueprint.json exitCriteria states 'the number is chosen when there is evidence from real journeys, not now', and this reconciliation preserves that honesty rather than inventing a number.

personalizationPlan.rule: Every personalised slot must have a neutral value that keeps the English correct, exactly as the semantic layer already enforces for Pre-A1. An arc that cannot run without a remembered fact is a broken arc.
personalizationPlan.invariant: Personalization may change what the conversation is ABOUT. It may never change canDoId, evaluation intent, mastery threshold, required evidence, prerequisite graph, XP/reward for equivalent work, whether a required capability can be skipped, or the grammar/vocabulary burden expected for the level (master contract section 7).
personalizationPlan.topicDiversityExpectation: governed by the shared topic-diversity policy (master contract section 8: explicit interests appear often enough to feel personal, the same interest does not dominate consecutive sessions, neutral real-life contexts remain present) — this is shared/core engine behaviour, not an A1-specific rule, and A1 does not override it.

fourStrandsAudit.meaningFocusedInput: present throughout via scene/comprehension/story steps; heaviest in finding_your_way (comprehending real, partly-unknown answers) and the daily_rhythm/finding_your_way/making_arrangements hosted stories
fourStrandsAudit.meaningFocusedOutput: the level's dominant strand — every arc's evidence target is an unaided statement or question in a real communicative frame
fourStrandsAudit.languageFocusedLearning: concentrated early: work_and_study introduces the level's core statement frame, daily_rhythm is explicitly the level's densest pattern moment (three new pattern groups); density drops through the middle arcs and is near zero in the closing arcs
fourStrandsAudit.fluencyDevelopment: strongest in the closing episodes of each arc (integration/consolidation episodes carry a newLanguageBudget near zero) and across the whole of making_arrangements, which introduces almost nothing new and holds prior language together under a withheld model answer
fourStrandsAudit.outOfScope: listening, speaking and pronunciation remain separate future capabilities per master contract section 13 and the CLAUDE.md voice/media boundary; A1 implements and tests only reading/meaning-focused input, written meaning-focused output, chat/roleplay interaction, form-focused learning and written fluency development

interactionDiscourseMediation.turnTakingAndRepair: inherits Pre-A1's ask_for_repair and adds two new repair frames (ask_meaning, ask_how_to_say); repair is planted by design in the early/mid arcs and learner-chosen by the late arcs
interactionDiscourseMediation.conversationLength: grows from 6 meaningful turns (work_and_study) to 12 (making_arrangements), staying within the level's own ceiling of one situation and one topic
interactionDiscourseMediation.discourseCoherence: single-topic by design at A1 (interactionCeiling); no A1 arc requires the learner to follow a topic change, which is explicitly deferred (cannotYet: 'sustain a conversation that changes topic more than once')
interactionDiscourseMediation.summarizationOrMediationTasks: none — mediation-like tasks (summarizing/simplifying for another person) are not an A1 capability; the master contract lists mediation as an available text-first mode in principle (section 13) but A1's arcs do not need it, and no mediation intent is proposed here
interactionDiscourseMediation.registerAndPragmatics: minimal at A1: polite forms inherited from Pre-A1 (polite_request, close_an_encounter); no register distinction is taught or assessed, consistent with the level's ceiling

deferredToA2.why: A second tense doubles every pattern the level owns. It is the first A2 capability precisely because it is the obvious next unlock.
A present tense with a time word already arranges things. going_to adds a form without adding a function A1 needs.
because turns one clause into two. Choice and preference work without it at this level.
Asking where something is and understanding a short answer is the autonomy; left/right/straight sequences are a comprehension load of their own.
One attribute is enough for A1 (She's a student). Adjective order, plurals and there is/are belong together, later.
Heard throughout A1, produced in A2. The morphology costs more than the capability it adds while is covers most needs.
Days of the week serve arrangements. Dates need ordinals and a second number system.
The alphabet is a system, not a phrase, and it pays off mainly with contact details this product does not collect.
A new context with its own vocabulary, when the transactional muscle A1 builds is already exercised by a shop and a counter.
Choosing works with this one at A1. Comparison is a structure with no A1 function.
Two adverbs make a routine truthful. Four make a grammar exercise.
Deliberate product decision: the curriculum never trains a learner to type real personal data.

optionalOrNotTaken.why: Cheap to say and rarely needed to act. Available as receptive input inside personal exchanges; not a required production.
Trimmed from the required set in review: He's a student already carries the function, and adjectives invite a catalogue.
A vocabulary set looking for a capability. If choosing ever needs it, this one is doing the work.
Mostly interface language, which the product already localises.

humanPilotQuestions: does the can/can't ability-vs-request disambiguation feel natural to a real beginner once arc what_you_can_do ships, or does it produce confusing corrections?

does arrange_to_meet feel genuinely A1-appropriate to real beginners, or does fixing a day/time/place in one held conversation feel like an A2-level task despite the tight ceiling (see cefrCaveats.arrangeToMeet)?

do the two single-appearance transactional capabilities (ask_the_price, buy_something) need a second live exposure earlier than the review scheduler alone provides, once real delayed-retention data exists?
does daily_rhythm's density (three new pattern groups in one arc, the level's admitted densest moment) produce measurable frustration or dropout compared to lighter arcs?
does light personalization on paying_and_choosing and what_you_can_do feel personal to a real learner, or repetitive across sessions?

does withholding the model answer by default in the late arcs (what_you_can_do, making_arrangements) measurably affect confidence or completion, compared to the early/mid arcs' more available support?

risks.risk: The level slides into topic units — food, family, clothes.
risks.mitigation: Every arc names a communicative problem before a topic, and no arc exists for a vocabulary set.

risks.risk: Time, numbers, questions and third person all arriving at once.
risks.mitigation: One new pattern group per episode, two only on an integration episode; the number extension arrives as prices.

risks.risk: One intent per phrase would add thirty for twenty-one episodes.
risks.mitigation: Fourteen intents plus subtypes on existing ones; repair grows by repairKind, quantity by range.

risks.risk: Every scene word becoming a tracked item.
risks.mitigation: Days of the week and numbers 11-100 are one item each, as numbers_1_10 already is; receptive input is not granted.

risks.risk: Ability can colliding with Pre-A1's request can.
risks.mitigation: Documented as the level's one real evaluator debt; see coreEngineRequirements.canAmbiguity — the ability arc must resolve it with a rule, not a second intent.

risks.risk: Price and purchase appearing once each.
risks.mitigation: Both return as receptive input in the closing arc and are carried by the review scheduler; the should-have transport episode is the trim candidate.

risks.risk: Twenty-one episodes in one lazy chunk.

risks.mitigation: Arc-sized sprints, each finishing with complete locales; the i18n check already fails on a missing key.

risks.risk: arrange_to_meet may read closer to A2's goal-oriented co-operation band than A1's information-exchange band.
risks.mitigation: see cefrCaveats.arrangeToMeet; flagged for LC-BP-A2 and LC-AUD-001 rather than silently resolved here.
